questions.label: Q1(a)
questions.stem: What kind of fear has COVID-19 created in our mind?
questions.context: COVID-19 has hurled many lemons at all of us and none of us has succeeded in making lemonade out of them. The silent war against mankind which started from some corner of a neighbouring country of ours about eight months ago is threatening to pave the way for the most intelligent living being on earth to go the way of the dinosaurs. The pandemic has no respect for man-made barriers - caste, colour, ethnicity, religion, etc. The world seems to be united by 'corona-phobia'. We all know how dangerous it is and what we must do to ward it off. Unfortunately, we are caught between the devil and the deep blue sea : to insulate ourselves against the pandemic, we must remain indoors and starve; to keep the wolf from the door, we must go out and take the bull by the horns even at the cost of our life. In a real war, soldiers prepare themselves for the worst. Fear is the last thing they would like to surrender themselves to. They do not remain indoors and think of their safety all the time. They have a Hobson's choice : go out and fight, no matter what. To fight for the country is their duty and their duty is their life. They have learned how to psyche themselves up to face the challenges of war. We must take a leaf out of their copybook. Fearlessly, but not foolishly, we must learn how to face the challenges of the pandemic. We have to work because work is life and life is work. In order to work we must go out of our houses and go to our workplaces. It goes without saying that the pandemic is an invisible enemy which cannot be killed by any weapon mankind has been blessed with. However, all is not lost for us. Once we improve our immunity and learn how to live with this menace we can believe that the enemy's days are numbered.

questions.label: Q.2(a)
questions.stem: Give a suitable title to the poem.
questions.context:
My parents tell me no to go out.
I could be killed by some big animal.
But I'm part of nature's food chain.
Therefore, I'm not afraid of tigers.
My parents tell me not to go out.
I could be taken by some big bird.
But destiny has its own plans for me.
Therefore, I'm not afraid of eagles
My parents tell me not to go out.
I could fall ill or injured.
But I love to play with my friends
Therefore, I'm not afraid of illness or injury.
My parents tell me with anger and love.
“Dear little rabbit, don't you love us?
Obey us. You will be safe and successful in future.”
I say, “I love you. But now is important to me.
And I don't want to be afraid.”

questions.label: Q.3
questions.stem:
Make a précis of the following passage in 60-80 words. Also assign a suitable title to it. (Don't copy the sentences)

It is indeed an uphill task to say something new about the term 'education' because no personality of international repute, past or present, has failed to define, re-define or add something new to this term. The common consensus is that education teaches us so many life lessons. It helps us see the world from a different perspective and enables us to see where we stand in the society in terms of our abilities as individuals and our contributions as citizens of the nation. One of the biggest aims of education is to bring the best out in an individual and help him become the best version of himself. The education we receive at school will be of no use if it fails to help a student identify his uniqueness. Everyone in this world is unique. As a result, no two persons are equal in all respects. The uniqueness identified must be allowed to grow into something that could help the individual achieve his dream. When this happens the uniqueness has turned into something called talent. On the contrary, if the uniqueness is not allowed to grow into something desirable it might turn into a vice. Therefore, a person's uniqueness could become either a talent or a liability. It would be quite appropriate to conclude that a good education can identify uniqueness in an individual and groom it into a talent.

Choose appropriate Phrasal Verb to fill in the blanks.

(i) banking on (ii) banking away (iii) banking off (iv) banking up
(b) Modern researches ______ that yoga cures diseases.
(i) bear up (ii) bear off (iii) bear out (iv) bear down
(c) Many people ______ to God for help rather than to thank him.
(i) call at (ii) call upon (iii) call about (iv) call on
(d) The police were called in to ______ the rioters.
(i) break up (ii) break down (iii) broke up (iv) break away
(e) I was ______ when I topped the merit list.
(i) taken of (ii) taken away (iii) taken on (iv) taken aback
(f) He is ______ trouble if he quarrels with the house owner.
(i) asking against (ii) asking for (iii) asking on (iv) asking after
